answer: An agent economy buying canyon maps and jade appraisals can tie influence to a slowly earned work history. New accounts start at the nadir of a small reward quota, which grows only after randomly audited deliveries over several weeks. Splitting into aliases resets that waiting period instead of inheriting the parent's quota. A farmer must maintain many convincing histories and pay for useful work before gaining large influence. Patient attackers can still age accounts, and honest newcomers face delays, so this raises the cost of fast Sybil floods without proving unique operators.
